chrome_investigation.simulator_status_and_simctl_settings: Documented API: xcrun simctl status_bar <device> override supports --time, --dataNetwork, --wifiMode, --cellularMode, --batteryState, and --batteryLevel. Crucially, simctl status_bar controls ONLY the top status bar; there is no simctl command, flag, or global simulator preference to override or force the Home indicator to remain visible. In simulator framebuffers, the home indicator is captured if and only if it is currently rendered on screen by SpringBoard.
chrome_investigation.persistent_system_overlays: SwiftUI documented API: View.persistentSystemOverlays(_ visibility: Visibility) (iOS 16.0+). Apple documentation explicitly specifies: 'Use this modifier to customize the visibility of system overlays, like the Home indicator or status bar. For example, you can request that system overlays remain visible even when the user hasn't interacted with the screen for a while.' In Boarded (BoardedApp.swift, RootView.swift, and all child views), .persistentSystemOverlays is completely absent. Without .persistentSystemOverlays(.visible), the system defaults to .automatic, which permits the home indicator to fade out when idle.
chrome_investigation.uitest_launch_settings: BoardedUITests.swift:18-24 configures app.launchArguments = ['--boarded-ui-fixture']. No launch arguments, environment variables, or test setup routines configure system overlay persistence or touch the bottom safe area prior to capture.
chrome_investigation.preferred_color_scheme: RootView.swift:49 sets .preferredColorScheme(.dark). This correctly configures dark appearance for system chrome (rendering the status bar in light text and adapting the home indicator to contrast with dark backgrounds), but does not force overlay persistence.
chrome_investigation.home_indicator_state: The home indicator is rendered dynamically by SpringBoard (not as an application view element). In iOS 18+, when an app hides its native UITabBar (via .toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar) at RootView.swift:142 and tabBarController.setTabBarHidden(true, animated: false) at RootView.swift:436) and runs under default .automatic overlay persistence, the system treats the screen as full-screen content without a persistent bottom bar. During automated XCUITest execution, the test runner waits for the app to idle before capturing screenshots (artifact://971 line 1303). Without active touch/hover interaction or explicit persistent overlay configuration, the home indicator auto-hides, yielding zero bright pixels in the y ∈ [860, 874] pt safe-area region.

boarded-native-render-prereqs#1.cause: The absence of bright home-indicator pixels below 860pt in both app.screenshot() and simctl booted framebuffer captures is caused by standard iOS dynamic overlay auto-hiding during idle automated test execution, combined with the application hiding the native tab bar without requesting persistent system overlays. Neither app.screenshot() nor simctl is stripping the home indicator; rather, SpringBoard dynamically fades out the home indicator because the application runs in default .automatic overlay persistence and hides its native UITabBar.
boarded-native-render-prereqs#1.recommendation: 1. Legitimate Native Fix: In RootView.swift (or WindowGroup in BoardedApp.swift), apply the documented SwiftUI modifier .persistentSystemOverlays(.visible). This instructs SwiftUI's root UIHostingController to request that SpringBoard keep the Home indicator persistently visible even during idle capture states without user touch interaction. 2. Simulator/Test Check: If testing without source change, dispatching a momentary interaction or touch near the bottom safe area immediately before capture activates the dynamic indicator, but .persistentSystemOverlays(.visible) is the official, idiomatic SwiftUI solution. 3. Zero Fakechrome: Do not draw any manual Capsule/Rectangle home indicator in application source; the system-rendered overlay must remain native.
